newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBJ sees end-March capital adequacy ratio at 10%.
newsitem.headline: IBJ sees end-March capital adequacy ratio at 10%.

text.p: The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) said on Monday it forecast its capital adequacy ratio would be 10 percent at the end of March 1997.
Under rules set by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), Japanese banks operating internationally must have capital equivalent to eight percent of risk-weighted assets.
IBJ forecasts a parent operating profit of 200 billion yen for the full business year to March 31, 1997, the official said.
The bank had almost completed its plans for writing off its bad loans by the end of March 1996, he added.
